key: I will declare the manly deeds of Indra, the first that he achieved, the Thunder-wielder. He slew the Dragon, then disclosed the waters, and cleft the channels of the mountain torrents.
s: Opening a hymn on Indra’s fight with Vrtra, the singer announces the god’s first deeds; Sāyaṇa, on 1.32.1, takes ‘the Dragon’ as the cloud and counts three deeds: slaying the cloud, bringing the waters down to earth, and setting the mountain rivers flowing.
src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 1.32.1, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 403053 (2024)

evidence.words: कानि वीर्याणीति तदुच्यते । "अहिं मेघम् "अहन् हतवान् । तदेतदेकं वीर्यम् । "अनु पश्चात् “अपः जलानि “ततर्द हिंसितवान् भूमौ पातितवानित्यर्थः । इदं द्वितीयं वीर्यम् । "पर्वतानां संबन्धिनीः “वक्षणाः प्रवहणशीलाः नदीः “प्र “अभिनत् भिन्नवान् कूलद्वयकर्षणेन प्रवाहितवानित्यर्थः । इदं तृतीयं वीर्यम् ।
evidence.gloss: Which valorous deeds? That is now told. He slew the ahi, the cloud: that is one deed. Afterwards he struck the waters, that is, made them fall to the ground: this is the second deed. He split the flowing rivers of the mountains, that is, set them flowing by cutting through their two banks: this is the third deed.

reason: The problem holds as a consistency matter. Hymn 1.32 in day.js prints Griffith’s “Vṛitra” (1.32.5 to 1.32.11) and 1.33.13 prints “Vrtra”; day 7 of this batch writes “Vrtra” twice. The sentence’s “Vritra” matched neither form on the day, so it is changed to “Vrtra” and nothing else. Evidence unchanged and re-found in packet.js veda 4 --verse 1.32.1. verse.js ok (Rig Veda 1.32.1, at [31,1]); entry-check ok.
